name: Aner
overview: Aner was a male Amorite known as "the Amorite" as referenced in Genesis 14:13. He is identified primarily by his tribal affiliation and gender. There are no additional notes recorded about his life or character in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Aner appears once in Scripture, specifically in Genesis 14:13, without any given meaning or title. It is presented simply as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Aner is explicitly identified as the brother of Mamre and Eshcol, forming a familial triad. He is also considered a descendant of Amor, inferred by his Amorite tribal affiliation. Additionally, Aner is noted as an ally of Abram, indicating a significant partnership in the biblical narrative.
scriptureSignificance: Aner's significance in Scripture lies in his alliance with Abram during a critical moment recorded in Genesis 14:13. As an Amorite and brother to Mamre and Eshcol, Aner's support of Abram highlights the cooperation between Abram and local tribal leaders. This alliance reflects the broader narrative of Abram's influence and relationships in the land.
